messages:
jess: FYI saw a regression in P50 throughput on the 2pm rollout. ~12% drop, coincides with the new admission-policy tweak for cache-hit batching.
ryan: ugh. which nodes/region? any obvious hot paths in the profile?
jess: eu-west-1 heavy, but observed across regions. quick top-line from profiler: more small batches (1-3 sequences) and increased kernel launch overhead. KV cache hit rate up ~18% after the prefix cache change, but packing underfilled.
omar: that matches a hypothesis: prefix cache hits reduce remaining token length so token-budget-based packing ends up with tiny leftover budgets and avoids coalescing. Did we change hit scoring recently?
jess: we made cache-hit responses mark remaining_tokens=0 earlier in the request lifecycle (to let low-latency returns bypass batching). result: continuous batcher sees many items with very small token estimates and admits them with priority.
elena: any kernel fallbacks noted? short sequences often pick the 'small-seq' kernel which has higher per-call overhead on Ampere for our model (we profiled that last quarter).
jess: yes, kernel selection flip was visible. trace snippet: 
```
# simplified trace (per-request)
request A: cache_hit=true, predicted_rem_tokens=2 -> admitted early -> kernel small-seq (launch 1.8ms)
request B: cache_miss, rem_tokens=120 -> waits -> packed with other misses -> kernel long-seq (amortized 0.6ms)
```
ryan: so cache hits are inflating the number of tiny launches. two levers: delay admitted cache-hits slightly to allow coalescing OR adjust token_budget logic to treat hit responses as packable with a reduced weight.
omar: propose a hybrid token bin policy: assign effective_token_cost = max(remaining_tokens, hit_multiplier * original_prompt_len). For hits, hit_multiplier could be 0.25 so they still pack. Also add a soft delay window (eg 2-4ms) for hit-path responses to let nearby requests join.
jess: prototyped config below and ran a quick A/B on a small fleet:
```
continuous_batching:
  token_budget_target: 800
  token_bins: [64, 128, 256, 512]
  hit_policy:
    enabled: true
    hit_multiplier: 0.3
    soft_delay_ms: 3
  admission:
    min_batch_size: 6
    allow_underfill_if_latency_breached: true
```
jess: result: underfill rate down from 38% -> 12%, P50 back within 1% of baseline, P95 unchanged. CPU/GPU kernel launch overhead reduced.
elena: nice. did you check edge cases where soft_delay adds tail latency for single-user requests?
jess: yes, we gated soft_delay by client_tier: realtime clients (tier=low-latency) bypass the soft delay. default customers get the pack-friendly behavior.
ryan: do we need to change rollout to include kernel-selector hints? if we can bias kernel selection by expected final sequence length (after hits), we can reduce the penalty.
omar: kernel hints sound good but invasive. cheaper change is to change the packer to compute effective_token_cost that includes a small fixed overhead per-request (to account for kernel-launch cost) so the binning is less sensitive to tiny remaining_tokens. e.g. effective = remaining_tokens + launch_overhead_tokens (say 12).
jess: we combined both: effective_token_cost = remaining_tokens + (is_hit ? hit_multiplier * prompt_len : launch_overhead_tokens). That seems to make packing more stable across mixes.
ryan: awesome. what's the plan for metrics and rollout? I want automated alarms if underfill rises or kernel-launch rate spikes.
jess: added new dashboard tiles: underfill_rate, avg_batch_fill_pct, kernel_launch_per_min, p50/p95 per-tenant. rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 6 hours with quick rollback if underfill > 25% or P50 regresses > 3%.
elena: please add a short note in the runbook about the cache-hit soft-delay so oncall knows to check hit-adjustment flag if we see weird latency.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary group (fleet-id s-112) starts at 2025-10-12T15:00Z. Automated rollback triggers configured.
jess: I'll push the config change to the feature-flag and a small unit test for effective_token_cost. thanks all — will post follow-up perf graphs once 25% canary completes. :thumbsup:
